# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 63 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 63 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_063_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 1 — Keep the Flesh Pure

**63:1** As I was sitting at home and glorifying God for all that I had seen, and meditating on the commandments — how they were beautiful and powerful and glad and glorious and able to save the soul of a man — I said to myself: I shall be blessed if I walk in these commandments, and blessed shall be all who walk in them.

**63:2** While I was saying these things to myself, I saw him sitting beside me and saying: "Why are you double-minded about the commandments that I gave you? They are beautiful. Do not be in any doubt, but clothe yourself with the faith of the Lord and walk in them, for I will strengthen you in them."

**63:3** "This commandment especially pleases me, lord," I said, "for I have never in my life sinned against it." "Speak," he said. "I have always," I said, "even to this day, kept myself chaste — from women and from every kind of adultery and impurity." He rejoiced at this and said: "I say this because you have done well in this. But I will tell you one more thing: you must also guard the flesh pure and undefiled, so that the Spirit that dwells in it may bear witness to it, and your flesh may be justified."

**63:4** "Take care," he said, "lest any thought should enter your heart concerning this flesh of yours and you suppose it to be defiled. For if the pure flesh is defiled by an evil thought, it brings death. But keep it pure, and believe that if you keep the flesh pure, you shall live to God."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the flesh-purity theology of the Similitude 6 transition.*
